castle_forms: a four-level sandcastle built into the side of a tomb

traversal: A sandstorm cycle blinds the approach every six hours.
The plain between settlement and castle is patrolled by something that hunts by vibration.
The castle moves. Its route is predictable; its schedule is not.
A dry riverbed is the only cover, and it floods without warning.

an ice-choked strait

a brine lake, heavier than water, floating things that should sink

a drowned cathedral, the nave still full of air
an iceberg hollowed into a palace
traversal: The castle is at lethal depth. Breath, pressure, and cold all need solving.
Nothing on the surface is safe after dark; the water glows where they hunt.
The only vessels belong to a faction that charges in favors, not gold.
Tides expose the approach for ninety minutes twice a day.

biomes: a desert basin beneath an endless sky
a cloud plateau with islands of rock

a mountain of kites and cables

castle_forms: a dirigible fortress of scrap metal, thousands of feet up
a kite city tethered to a mountain
a citadel on a floating rock, moored by chains
a nest-tower of bone and rope
a cloud-keep that solidifies only at dusk
a crashed sky-ark, half its decks still airworthy
traversal: The castle floats. Reaching it needs flight, a captured airship, or a very bad idea.
The wind at altitude tears anything unanchored off the rock.
The castle drops bombs on anything that gathers in the open.
The tethers are the only way up, and they are guarded from above.

biomes: a necropolis of layered tombs

a mine that was dug from the bottom up
an ossuary maze built from a single enormous skeleton
a fungal cathedral with its own weather
a buried city, streets intact, sky of stone
castle_forms: a crypt-palace of trapped corridors and false thrones
a keep carved downward into a shaft
a fortress of living stone that reshapes itself
a hive-palace of wax and bone
a temple at the bottom of a pit, reachable by stair or by falling
a mine-lord's manor built across a chasm
traversal: Every corridor is trapped. The traps are the castle's real garrison.
There is no map; the tunnels reorder when nobody is looking.
Air runs out in the deep sections. Bring light and a clock.
The approach passes through the faction's burial grounds; they take that personally.

FACTION_WANT: a piece of an artifact held in another quadrant
to breach the dome and leave
revenge for a massacre the others deny
a marriage alliance nobody else wants
TENSION: {A} and {B} have been at war for a generation over {W}; {C} sells to both sides.
{A} holds the throne of one castle and {B} wants it; {C} is neutral until someone pays.
{A} and {B} are allied against {C}, whose castle nobody has breached. The alliance is one insult from collapsing.
All three want {W}. Two of them will ally with crawlers. The third will pretend to.
{A} secretly serves {C}. {B} suspects. The crawlers will be asked to prove it.
STORYLINE: An artifact in three pieces, one in each faction's keeping. Assembled, it does something the dungeon won't describe.
A mad mage has turned himself into an elemental and is the real power behind one castle.
A feral god's egg is buried under the neutral quadrant. Every faction knows. None of them will say it.
The dome is failing early. The factions blame each other. The clock on the wall is wrong.
One faction's ruler is a former crawler from a past season. They remember the rules better than you do.
The castles' thrones are linked: sit on one and the other three rulers feel it.
THRONE_NOTE: The throne is real. Sitting on it counts. Standing next to it does not.
The throne room is above the stairwell, not beside it. Take the room, then find the trapdoor.
The throne is occupied by something that is not the boss. Killing it still counts.
Throne room doors seal when the boss drops below half. Nobody in, nobody out.
Two thrones. One is a mimic. The dungeon finds this very funny.
The throne room is flooded to the waist. The stairwell is dry. Nobody knows how.
APPROACH: Front gate is a killing field; the service entrance is real but guarded by the faction that built it.
The garrison rotates every twelve hours; the changeover is the window.
A civilian population lives inside. Collateral is on the crawlers.
The castle's defenses are automated and stupid. Its ruler is not.
There is a traitor inside who will open a door, once, for a price.
Nothing inside is hostile until the throne room. Then all of it is.
OBSTACLE: A hangar/dock full of the castle's vehicles, crewed and fueled.
A great hall of feasting guests who are also the garrison.
A puzzle door keyed to the faction's language.
A vault of cages; what's inside can be freed or used.
A chapel where the faction's god actually answers.
A bridge that only bears the weight of one crawler at a time.
An armory. Everything in it is trapped, and everything in it is good.

DIFFICULTY: Meant to fall first. A competent party can take it in a day.
Needs preparation or a faction ally, not a miracle.
Needs the bubble's other resources: vehicles, allies, or numbers.
Designed to be last. Expect to lose people.
BUBBLE_STATE: Mostly under-leveled and directionless; a handful of competent teams are hoarding gear.
Split into two camps that won't share a safe room.
Led, badly, by whoever shouted first.
Twenty of them are a single well-run guild who consider the rest ballast.
Thinning fast. The count on the safe-room screen drops every hour.
One famous name in the bubble, and everyone is waiting for them to solve it.
RIVALS: a top-ten crawler with a bounty and a temper
a trap specialist who works alone
a duo of siblings who have already taken one castle and won't say how
a leaderboard hunter looking for boss kills
nobody worth naming, which is its own problem
GUARDIAN_POSTS: It holds the only way in.
It circles the castle and goes for anything that comes close.
It sleeps in the courtyard and wakes for anything louder than a whisper.
It guards the castle's vehicles, and counts them every hour.
It patrols the edge of the quadrant, where the dome comes down.
It keeps the gate and has never once been off duty.
It guards a vault the ruler has forgotten about.
It hunts the open ground between the settlements and the castle.
It lives in the castle's lowest level and comes up when the ruler calls.

templates.title: Free {npc}
templates.objective: {npc}, one of the {faction}, is held in the cells under {castle} in the {quadrant} quadrant. Get them out alive.

templates.title: Find Out Who Killed My Son
templates.objective: {giver_s} son was found dead outside {rival_home}. The {rival} swear they had nothing to do with it. Find out who did.

templates.title: Kill {npc}
templates.objective: {npc} of the {rival} has to die before the bubble pops. Nobody is to know who asked.

templates.title: Stay Out of {place}
templates.objective: Stay out of {place} until the bubble pops. That's the whole quest. It is harder than it sounds.

templates.title: Get {creature}
templates.objective: {creature}, the {faction_s} {creature_what}, got loose in the {quadrant} quadrant. Bring it back alive. It bites.

templates.title: The {Item} Job
templates.objective: Steal {item} from {castle} before {ruler} notices it's gone, and bring it to {giver}.

templates.title: The Hidden Shrine
templates.objective: The {rival} keep a shrine hidden somewhere in the {quadrant} quadrant. Find it, and tell nobody but {giver}.

templates.title: Peace Talks
templates.objective: Escort {giver} to {rival_home} and back, and keep the peace while the {faction} and the {rival} talk.

templates.title: Thin the Herd
templates.objective: Kill thirty {mob} in the {quadrant} quadrant. {giver} will know if you're lying.

templates.title: Hold the Throne
templates.objective: Take the throne room of {castle} and keep it until the {faction} arrive to claim it.

templates.title: Turncoat
templates.objective: {npc} of the {rival} wants to defect. Get them out of {rival_home} without the {rival} noticing.

templates.title: The Ruler's Ear
templates.objective: Get an audience with {ruler}, who rules {castle}, and deliver the {faction_s} terms. Survive the reply.

the key to the castle's lowest cell

rewards: a Silver Quest Box and the {faction_s} inn free for the rest of the floor
a Gold Quest Box and a favor from the {faction}
a Bronze Quest Box and a guide through the {faction_s} lands
a Silver Quest Box and the {faction_s} help with your castle
flavor: The {faction} have asked three other parties. None of them came back to say no.
Whoever posted this has crossed out the reward twice and written it in larger.
It is a simple job, they say, the way people say that about the jobs that aren't.
The {rival} would pay more for you to fail. Nobody has told you that.
There is a deadline. It has not been mentioned.
Half the {faction} want this done. The other half want it done quietly.
The last crawler who took this one is now a cautionary tale with a statue.
The quest text has been translated from the {faction_s} language, badly.
It pays on completion, and the {faction} define completion generously.
Nobody in the settlement will meet your eye while you hold this one.
Somebody has scratched GOOD LUCK into the notice. It does not read as sincere.
The reward is real. The {faction_s} account of events is decoratively arranged.
